title: What If You Froze Solid for Six Hours? In 1980 a Teenager Did, and Lived

scenes.text: What if you froze stiff as a board, no pulse, for six hours? One teenager woke up.
December 20, 1980, Lengby, Minnesota. Jean Hilliard's car slides into a ditch at 30 below Celsius. She walks off in cowboy boots.
She collapses near a farmhouse. Six hours later rancher Wally Nelson finds her: eyes frozen open, stiff as a board, bubbles at her nose.
At the hospital: no pulse, no blood pressure, too cold for the thermometer. Needles snap on her skin.
The doctors expect her to die. They wrap her in heating pads anyway. By noon, she's talking.
Cold slows the body like hibernation, so the brain needs far less oxygen. Nobody is dead until warm and dead. She went home with blistered toes.

description:
What if you froze solid? On 20 December 1980, 19-year-old Jean Hilliard crashed her car near Lengby, Minnesota, at about minus 30 Celsius and lay in the snow for six hours before rancher Wally Nelson found her frozen stiff, eyes open, with no pulse.
Her body was too hard for an IV needle and too cold for the thermometer, yet after doctors warmed her with heating pads she was talking by noon and left with only blistered toes. Cold slows the body like hibernation, so the brain needs far less oxygen, the reason doctors say nobody is dead until they're warm and dead.

first_comment: Her body was so stiff she wouldn't fit in the truck cab, so the rancher drove her in her own car. Which survival story should we run through next?
